rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - two-season (2014, 2015) mini-lysimeter experiment in Karaj, Iran comparing surface drip (DI) and subsurface drip (SDI) on forage corn, three replicates each. Q2: Table 4 and Results - WUE of corn was 8.32 kg/m3 under SDI versus 6.67 under DI (mean of two years; 7.96 vs 6.14 in 2014, 8.68 vs 7.20 in 2015), significantly different. Q4: Table 2 and Results - soil evaporation measured with unplanted mini-lysimeters was lower under SDI (157.6 mm) than DI (197.9 mm) while transpiration was higher under SDI; authors attribute the lower ETc-act and better WUE under SDI mainly to reduced soil surface evaporation.
rows.notes: WUE derived from one method (biomass / water-balance ETc-act in mini-lysimeters); no second independent method. Single site, loamy soil, one crop, one cultivar; two years are not sites. Measurements at mini-lysimeter scale within an 18-ha farm, not farm-scale results. No conditions for the effect stated from own findings (the semi-arid/high-evaporation context is cited from other work). No limitations of the study stated. Only LSD letter groupings; no SD, SE, CI or range reported for WUE.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - two-season mini-lysimeter field experiment comparing DI and SDI on corn in Karaj, Iran.
rows.notes: Weed occurrence was not measured or reported in this study. The only mention is in the abstract's research highlights, which attribute SDI superiority to more favorable soil moisture and low weed incidence, but no weed data, method or results appear in the Methods, Results or any table/figure. The study measured ETc-act, E, Tp, crop coefficients, LAI, height, stem diameter, biomass and WUE. The claim that weed occurrence was reduced under SDI is therefore not supported by an own result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - two-season (2014, 2015) replicated mini-lysimeter experiment comparing DI and SDI on forage corn. Q2: Table 4 and Results - biomass yield was 81.90 ton/ha under SDI compared with 63.21 ton/ha under DI (77.36 vs 60.18 in 2014; 86.44 vs 66.24 in 2015), significantly different; LAI, height and stem diameter were also higher under SDI. Q4: Table 2 and Results - plant transpiration (ETc-act minus measured soil evaporation) was higher under SDI (250.1 mm, 65% of ETc-act) than DI (221.8 mm, 52%), and LAI was higher under SDI (4.6 vs 3.4 at mid-season), presented as the pathway for higher biomass.
rows.notes: Yield measured by a single method (harvest biomass in mini-lysimeters). Single site, soil, crop and cultivar. Lysimeter-scale result only. The authors explain the yield advantage by optimal root-zone moisture status but root-zone soil moisture comparison is not reported; the measured intermediate is transpiration/LAI. No support conditions stated from own findings; no limitations stated; letter groupings only, no dispersion measure for yield.

notes: Full text appears complete. Primary two-year mini-lysimeter study (Karaj, Iran, loamy soil, forage corn) comparing surface and subsurface drip; reports ET components, crop coefficients, growth indices, biomass yield and WUE. No weed measurements despite the highlight statement.
